newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil downgraded to neutral.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Brazil downgraded to neutral.

text.p: -- Robert Fleming said on Monday it had downgraded Brazil to neutral from overweight in its model portfolio of Latin American stocks.

-- Analysts Omar Borla and Walter Stoeppelwerth wrote in a report they reduced the rating because of concerns about Brazil's trade deficit. The trade shortfall reached $1.3 billion in October, well above most analysts' estimates.
-- They said Brazil might be forced to deal with the deficit by spurring exports through devaluation of the real, its currency.

-- "We expect that an acceleration in the exchange rate devaluation will pre-empt the market's fear that the perpetual appreciation of the real will eventually lead to a maxi-devaluation," Borla and Stoeppelwerth wrote.
-- They also said the Central Bank could try to deal with the deficit by limiting consumer credit and other measures.
-- "We think the next two months are a perfect time to sit back and wait for buying opportunities or a clear signal that local sentiment is improving."
